scope: Local independent security and correctness review of the additive Hub r36 Wi-Fi catalog patch. No server or device calls, writes, deployment, or container restart.

independent_execution.fixtures: Synthetic workspace data only; actual FastAPI handlers, actual AESGCM, actual SQLite scope resolver, and extracted existing FirmwareStorage.authenticate_device with synthetic DB/token helpers. TestClient uses in-process ASGI transport.
independent_execution.fixture_path_policy: Short workspace .tmp/hub-central-independent-fixtures-20261105 scratch, unique per-test child, resolved-parent assertion before cleanup, bytecode disabled. Existing auth source is resolved from the workspace root.

verified_cases: Actual system assignment resolver shares only within the active assigned system and denies revoked, inactive, unassigned, and cross-system access.
Actual existing approved-device authentication callback is reused; ambiguous matching token hashes are rejected.
Missing or invalid bearer, insecure HTTP, query-based scope, and disabled capture endpoints fail closed; successful catalog response is no-store.
Ciphertext is encrypted at rest with fresh nonces; scope-bound AESGCM AAD rejects ciphertext transplantation without leaking the synthetic PSK.
Replacing the encryption key with another valid 32-byte key cannot append a new scope or mutate the existing catalog. Global key_id is checked against one key-byte snapshot used by AESGCM.
Concurrent CAS writes have exactly one winner and advance the canonical revision by one.
A later invalid record makes a multi-record merge atomic with byte-identical original file; errors do not echo secrets.
Existing-credential replacement requires an explicit replacement choice or fresh client-reported connected provenance with CAS; stale provenance is rejected.
The server revision counter is independent of untrusted client revision, including the maximum incoming integer boundary.
Canonical origin is the authenticated owner and cannot be forged by submitted record metadata.
Duplicate JSON keys and oversized bodies are rejected before mutation.
Init-only refuses an existing key or catalog and preserves the existing bytes.

static_review.main_integration: Four additive integrations preserve the existing firmware router and middleware, reuse existing FirmwareStorage.authenticate_device and DB resolver, require HTTPS, and explicitly set enable_captures=False.
static_review.scope: Server-side system:<positive systems.id> resolution requires approved device and active assigned system. There is no global approved-device catalog fallback.
static_review.store: Canonical schema-2 credentials.json has isolated encrypted scopes and a SHA256 key_id. Secret key and catalog are owner-private 0600 with private directories; existing parent ownership/modes are preserved.
static_review.locking_and_atomicity: Read/CAS/encrypt/atomic catalog replacement occurs under the shared store lock. Error messages are bounded static codes rather than exception or request-body contents.
static_review.provenance_limit: Fresh connected provenance is an authenticated client report, not an independent server measurement of Wi-Fi success. Saved NM timestamps are not proof of a working password.
static_review.dependencies: Existing downloaded r36 security.py already imports cryptography serialization and Ed25519 and existing main imports security. The additive Dockerfile reuses the operator-verified current r36 image; it does not install a new dependency set.
static_review.captures: Disabled in the actual main integration and default router. Capture readiness is outside this independent sign-off.

resolved_blockers: Untrusted incoming revision previously could overflow the usable canonical counter; server-counter-only increment is now tested.

A replaced valid encryption key previously could create a new scope in the old catalog. The independent regression reproduced HTTP 200 instead of 503 on the superseded module; the pinned 410f module now passes the regression.
limits: No live Hub, device, DNS, TLS proxy, Docker image build, container switch, or authenticated production request was executed by the reviewer.

Linux ownership, mode, flock, fsync, crash durability and real persistent-volume behavior require the separately guarded deployment and runtime checks; Windows fixture tests do not establish those properties on the production host.
Deployment must use the final pinned module and a matching initialized schema-2 catalog/key binding; superseded ad70 artifacts are not covered by this sign-off.
This review does not qualify universal USB, capture storage, local data deletion, or physical detector performance.
